Method of Attack: The attacker published three malicious versions of the package, which contained code that triggered the download of a remote malicious script during installation. It was suspected that the maintainer's account was hijacked due to password leakage or being cracked.
Impacted Systems: Nearly 1000 other third-party packages that depend on this package
Attack Vector: The attacker first modified the scripts field in package.json to trigger the execution of the malicious script before the package was installed. In the malicious version, three new files were updated, namely preinstall.js, preinstall.bat, preinstall.sh. They judged the system platform and executed corresponding scripts. On the Windows platform, the script also downloaded a Trojan component.
Indicators of Compromise: http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension - the script downloads an executable file named 'jsextension' from this URL, which is then used to run mining services on the machine.
Addition of preinstall.js, preinstall.bat, and preinstall.sh files
